text:
Cory: Quick thread — we keep hitting inconsistencies between the policy engine's hedging windows and what the runtime actually does. My sketch: add explicit lifecycle phases to policy manifests (draft/canary/active/retire) and a tiny versioned lease so runtimes know when to honor hedge windows vs. ignore them. Thoughts?
Meera: +1 on lifecycle phases. Current problem is operators tweak hedges during incidents and some runtimes apply stale windows for minutes. A lease with TTL would help.
Jules: How would lease be acquired/renewed? Central controller push or runtime pull? Pull makes private deployments easier.
Cory: leaning pull for Private (VPC) compatibility. Controller publishes manifest + seq, runtime polls /manifest/latest?lease. If lease seq matches local seq then runtime enforces canary windows, otherwise falls back to safe defaults.
Olivia: We need to define "safe defaults". For tiers the runtime should never hedge beyond X ms or beyond cost cap Y unless controller explicitly authorizes. Otherwise customer apps could spike spend.
Meera: Agreed. Proposal: runtime has two enforcement modes: strict (controller-signed lease present) and conservative (no lease). Conservative means single request hedges only for sub-ms fanout, no multi-tier hedges.
Jules: We also need an ABI between policy engine and runtime that avoids shipping policy language. Keep runtime dumb: it accepts a policy-hint blob {version, hedge_windows[], cost_cap} and returns telemetry/acceptance. Policy decisions and ordering stay in controller.
Olivia: That preserves the single source of truth. But for latency-critical fast-paths we might want runtime to make local micro-decisions (e.g., escalate from tier A->B if probe shows cold GPU). How do you reconcile?
Cory: idea: controller can mark some heuristics as "local_allowed" in manifest. Runtime can then trigger local-only short hedges (<10ms extra) but must emit an audit event with decision + reason. Controller can revoke local_allowed immediately via lease.
Meera: Audit events are key. We should sample heavy and send summaries to telemetry to avoid noise. Also include a decision_id per request so controller can correlate.
Jules: Example manifest snippet (rough):
```yaml
policy_version: 2026-03-01
lifecycle: canary
seq: 42
hedges:
  - tier: premium
    windows_ms: [2, 8]
    cost_cap_cents_per_1k: 60
    local_allowed: true
  - tier: standard
    windows_ms: [5]
    cost_cap_cents_per_1k: 30
lease_ttl_s: 30
```
Olivia: That looks good. Also include a `fallback_order` array so runtime knows which model variants are compatible for preemptive hedging.
Cory: Good call. Another tradeoff: sidecar vs library. Sidecar centralizes lease polling and auditing; library is simpler for bundle. Sidecar preferred for Dedicated and Hosted, library for small Private setups.
Meera: Sidecar gives us a single place to patch leases and rotate auth. If library enforces policy it needs to embed auth and poll logic which is a maintenance burden.
Jules: Implementation plan: 1) RFC that defines manifest fields + enforcement modes 2) sidecar prototype that implements lease polling + audit sink 3) runtime adapter shim that consumes sidecar hints 4) canary rollout on non-prod region.
Olivia: Ops concerns: when lease TTL lapses we must avoid capacity thrashing. Suggest exponential backoff on revocations and a short locking window so multiple runtimes don't mass-failover simultaneously.
Cory: Good. Add jitter to backoff and a per-tenant cooldown. Also, controller should be able to issue graceful retire transitions: canary->active requires a forced sync and an explicit commit endpoint.
eng-bot: @deploybot started canary of sidecar v0.1 in staging (job 87321). Logs: pod r3x2 reported manifest seq 42, lease ok.
Meera: For observability: status surface should show manifest.seq, lease_state, last_decision_id, sample_decisions_count, and a small histogram of hedging latency deltas. Make these per-tenant in console.
Jules: Also add a lint step in CI that rejects manifests with hedges that violate global cost guardrails (e.g., cost_cap > account_quota).
Olivia: Action items: Cory write RFC + manifest schema draft; Meera prototype sidecar polling + audit; Jules add CI lint rule; Olivia owns rollout plan and canary checklist.
Cory: I'll spin up an RFC doc today and link it. If no objections by EOD tomorrow we lock shape and start prototyping. :+1:
Meera: thanks — I'll start a minimal sidecar repo and push a README with polling flow and sampling knobs.
Jules: I'll draft the CI lint PR template.
Olivia: I'll coordinate with security for auth on manifest polling and with SRE for cooldown defaults.
Cory: Awesome. Closing loop here — RFC incoming.
